reviews.author: Mon Ami
reviews.text:
I am one of our customers who has been a regular customer for several years.
I use it often because it's close to my house, and even if the quality is sometimes poor, I just skip it because I think it's cost-effective.

However, there was a problem with the frozen mackerel I bought today, so I returned it for the first time, but I was very angry at the unpleasant response from the receptionist.

Because it was summer, I was worried about living things, so I bought frozen mackerel and stewed it at home, but the smell was so bad and the cooked fish tasted strange that it was difficult to eat.

So I returned the leftovers and the cooked ones, and the staff at the fishery corner smelled the returned items and asked what was the problem, raising their blood and making people feel weird by asking why they were doing this to something that was still good.

Who wouldn't find it inconvenient and frustrating to bring and return food that was painstakingly prepared in a heat wave?

Before telling the customer that there is no problem and raising the bar, shouldn't we recognize that there may be a problem with the frozen product even if it looks fine?

Depending on the person, they may be more or less sensitive to smells and tastes, but by my own standards, they are fine, so I don't think they are treating me like a strange guest.

reviews.author: Kim Jong-gyu
reviews.text:
Even though one of the employees at the vegetable part who speaks informally is upset because of complaints from other customers, you shouldn't do that. I asked carefully, but the answer was “Why?” I was still arguing with the customer, so I asked again later, and the response of “what” and the frowning and annoyed attitude was a rude and insincere attitude to treat people poorly, not to mention the customer. If you don't want to work like that, how about taking a break? When I asked him why he spoke informally and asked him to be polite, he even got angry in a hostile tone. It was completely unsatisfactory customer service. It's been a while since I had a really unpleasant and unpleasant experience. I returned home shocked by the isolated service, where one customer got offended and took out that negative feeling on another customer who looked younger than him. Please reflect. It seems like there is a need for that.

PS. Other than that, the other staff were friendly. Since the discomfort was caused by one person, please refrain from making hasty generalizations.

reviews.author: Jung hyun Kim
reviews.text:
After consultation, I purchased a location tracker for 418,000 won. The manual said that once registered, returns were not possible, so I downloaded the app and requested consultation because the explanation of the fee system for each model was not clear. I received a response in 6 days. I was unable to use the product within the desired period, and although they told me several times that they would give me an answer, there was no contact and the after-sales service was a mess, so I requested a refund, but after 7 days, they said no. Reported to Korea Consumer Agency.  If you go to places like Coupang, Danawa, and J Boss, there are many location trackers that are cheap and perform well. This company really has a bad conscience. It's not worth even one star.

I was dumbfounded after seeing the reply, so I edited the post again.

Even if they humbly accept their mistakes and apologize, it's not enough.
They do everything they can to avoid contact from the Consumer Agency after filing the case, such as by returning the registered mail. It's hard to believe that there are people doing business like this in Korea in 2025.
For the public interest, I will not stand still and report and post articles on the Internet that reveal the facts. I've been trying to be as polite as possible with numerous text messages, but I don't think they are people who deserve that kind of treatment.

These days, there are many sites with good devices at good prices.
If you go to Coupang alone, you can find self-defense cams priced in the tens of thousands of won.
There is absolutely no need to pay hundreds of thousands of won for these products.
Naver will protest that if they only pay advertising fees, they upload videos to these companies without reviewing them. Let's go to the end.
